chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed me, from Abu Ja'far ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan al-Nisaburi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from al-Zurari who said:
There is an occultation for the Qaim before his appearance. I asked: For what reason? He replied: He fears being killed.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim (the Rising One), a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.غَيْبَةً: Occultation, a period of concealment or absence

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam al-Qaim have an occultation before his appearance?
ai.summary: In this narration from Zurarah, a key companion of the Imams, the reason for the Imam al-Qaim's pre-appearance occultation is identified as fear of assassination (khawf al-qatl), reflecting the historical reality of political instability during the Minor Occultation. This highlights the protective wisdom behind the delay, ensuring the Imam's survival until the divinely appointed time for his global justice.
